svg.title: Two hypothetical similar ramp models with equal slope angles
svg.desc: Two separately scaled right triangles each have rise to horizontal run ratio one to twelve: model A has rise 0.4 metre and run 4.8 metres, model B has rise 1 metre and run 12 metres. Their corresponding horizontal runs have ratio 2 to 5. An equally valid common angle could use runs 4 metres and 10 metres, a rise to run ratio of one to ten. Thus the rise measurements and shared but unspecified angle determine the ratio of runs, not the actual runs. The diagram is a mathematical model only and does not certify accessibility or legal compliance.
svg.text: Same acute angle: a shared ratio, not a fixed run
The triangles are displayed at different scales for readability.

g.text: Chosen model: rise/run = 1/12 in both triangles; hence run A : run B = 2 : 5.
Alternative equal-angle pair: runs 4 m and 10 m also have ratio 2 : 5, at slope 1/10.
Without specifying the shared angle or one run, the individual runs are not determined.
Educational geometry example only. Ramp width, landings, rails, surfaces and current local rules need separate review.
